comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
comments.body: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` returns a Promise and can reject (e.g., insecure context, permissions, unsupported browser). The current `void ...` call neither awaits nor catches errors, and it sets `isCopied` to true even if the copy fails, which can also produce unhandled Promise rejections in the console. Consider making this handler `async`, guarding for `navigator.clipboard?.writeText`, awaiting it, and only entering the copied state on success (and optionally surfacing failures via `setErrorMessage`).

comments.author: chatgpt-codex-connector
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Gate success state on clipboard write completion**

The click handler marks the chip as copied immediately and ignores the `writeText` promise result, so users can see a “Copied!” confirmation even when the clipboard write fails (for example, permission denied, insecure context, or unsupported clipboard API). Because `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` is fire-and-forget here, failures are also unhandled, which can surface as runtime promise errors. Awaiting the write (or handling `.then/.catch`) before setting `isCopied` avoids false success feedback and prevents unhandled failures.
